paras.text: Body need a certain amount of iodine in order to make a chemical known as thyroid hormone. Thyroid hormone controls body metabolism and other important functions in the body.
paras.urdu: تھائرائیڈ ہارمون نامی کیمیائی مادہ بنانے کے لیے جسم کو آیوڈین کی ایک خاص مقدار درکار ہوتی ہے۔ تھائرائیڈ ہارمون جسم کے تحول اور دوسرے اہم افعال کو کنٹرول کرتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: بدن د تایرایډ هورمون په نوم کیمیاوي مادې د جوړولو لپاره یوه ټاکلې اندازه ایوډین ته اړتیا لري. د تایرایډ هورمون د بدن میتابولیزم او نور مهم فعالیتونه کنټرولوي.

paras.text: Iodine is found primarily in seawater and in the soil especially in coastal areas. At high elevations, iodine is often deficient in the water and soil. Lack of iodine can cause an abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as a goitre.
paras.urdu: آیوڈین بنیادی طور پر سمندری پانی اور مٹی، خصوصاً ساحلی علاقوں میں پائی جاتی ہے۔ بلند علاقوں کے پانی اور مٹی میں اکثر آیوڈین کی کمی ہوتی ہے۔ آیوڈین کی کمی سے تھائرائیڈ غدود غیر معمولی طور پر بڑھ سکتا ہے، جسے گلہڑ کہتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: ایوډین تر ډېره په سمندري اوبو او خاوره کې، په ځانګړي ډول په ساحلي سیمو کې، موندل کېږي. په لوړو سیمو کې په اوبو او خاوره کې ډېری وخت ایوډین کم وي. د ایوډین کمښت د تایرایډ غدې د غیرعادي غټېدو لامل کېدای شي، چې جاغور بلل کېږي.

paras.text: A goitre is an abnormal enlargement of thyroid gland. Thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland located at the base of neck. The most common cause of goitres worldwide is a lack of iodine in the diet. Iodine deficiency may be made worse by a diet high in hormone-inhibiting foods, such as cabbage, broccoli and cauliflower.
paras.urdu: گلہڑ تھائرائیڈ غدود کا غیر معمولی بڑھنا ہے۔ تھائرائیڈ تتلی نما غدود ہے جو گردن کی جڑ میں ہوتا ہے۔ دنیا بھر میں گلہڑ کی سب سے عام وجہ غذا میں آیوڈین کی کمی ہے۔ بند گوبھی، بروکلی اور پھول گوبھی جیسی ہارمون کو روکنے والی غذاؤں کی زیادہ مقدار آیوڈین کی کمی کو مزید خراب کر سکتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: جاغور د تایرایډ غدې غیرعادي غټېدل دي. تایرایډ د پروانې په شکل غده ده چې د غاړې په بېخ کې موقعیت لري. په نړۍ کې د جاغور تر ټولو عام لامل په غذا کې د ایوډین کمښت دی. د هورمون مخنیوونکو خوړو، لکه کرم، بروکلي او ګلپي، ډېر لرونکی خوراک د ایوډین کمښت لا خرابولای شي.

paras.text: Our body does not naturally make iodine, so the only way to get this nutrient is through diet. Adults typically require 150μg per day. Pregnant and breastfeeding women need 200μg per day.
paras.urdu: ہمارا جسم قدرتی طور پر آیوڈین نہیں بناتا، اس لیے یہ غذائی جز صرف خوراک سے حاصل ہوتا ہے۔ بالغوں کو عموماً روزانہ 150μg درکار ہوتی ہے۔ حاملہ اور دودھ پلانے والی خواتین کو روزانہ 200μg درکار ہوتی ہے۔

paras.text: 13.1.3.1 Structure

Sodium, magnesium and aluminium oxides consist of giant structures containing metal ions and oxide ions. Magnesium oxide is similar in structure to sodium chloride. The crystalline aluminium oxide is known as corundum, in which oxygen ions form nearly hexagonal close-packed structure with the aluminium ions.
paras.urdu: سوڈیم، میگنیشیم اور ایلومینیم کے آکسائیڈز بڑی ساختوں پر مشتمل ہیں، جن میں دھاتی اور آکسائیڈ آئن ہوتے ہیں۔ میگنیشیم آکسائیڈ کی ساخت سوڈیم کلورائیڈ جیسی ہے۔ قلمی ایلومینیم آکسائیڈ کورنڈم کہلاتی ہے، جس میں آکسیجن کے آئن ایلومینیم آئنوں کے ساتھ تقریباً مسدسی قریب قریب بھری ہوئی ساخت بناتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د سوډیم، مګنیزیم او المونیم اکسایډونه لوی جوړښتونه لري چې فلزي او اکسایډ ایونونه پکې دي. د مګنیزیم اکسایډ جوړښت د سوډیم کلورایډ په څېر دی. بلوري المونیم اکسایډ کورنډم بلل کېږي؛ پکې د اکسیجن ایونونه له المونیم ایونونو سره نږدې شپږګوټیز متراکم جوړښت جوړوي.

paras.text: The giant structures (the metal oxides and silicon dioxide) have high melting points and boiling points because a lot of energy is needed to break the strong bonds (ionic or covalent) operating in their lattices. The oxides of phosphorus, sulphur and chlorine consist of individual molecules, some small and simple, others polymeric.

paras.text: The attractive forces between these molecules will be dispersion forces and dipole-dipole interactions. The strength of the attractive forces depend on the size, shape and polarity of various molecules but are always much weaker than the ionic or covalent bonds present in a giant structure. These oxides are gases, liquids or low – melting solids.

Society, Technology And Science

Body need a certain amount of iodine in order to make a chemical known as thyroid hormone. Thyroid hormone controls body metabolism and other important functions in the body.

Iodine is found primarily in seawater and in the soil especially in coastal areas. At high elevations, iodine is often deficient in the water and soil. Lack of iodine can cause an abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as a goitre.

A goitre is an abnormal enlargement of thyroid gland. Thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland located at the base of neck. The most common cause of goitres worldwide is a lack of iodine in the diet. Iodine deficiency may be made worse by a diet high in hormone-inhibiting foods, such as cabbage, broccoli and cauliflower.

Our body does not naturally make iodine, so the only way to get this nutrient is through diet. Adults typically require 150μg per day. Pregnant and breastfeeding women need 200μg per day.

13.1.3 Physical Properties of the Oxides

The oxides of period 3ʳᵈ elements are following.

The oxides in the top row are the oxides where period 3 elements are in their highest oxidation state. In these oxides, all the outer electrons in period 3 elements are being involved in bonding from just one in sodium to all seven outer electrons of chlorine in Cl₂O₇.

The oxides (high oxidation state) of sodium, magnesium, aluminium, silicon, phosphorous are in solid state and those of sulphur and chlorine are in liquid state. The oxides having low oxidation state of sulphur and chlorine are in gaseous state.

13.1.3.1 Structure

Sodium, magnesium and aluminium oxides consist of giant structures containing metal ions and oxide ions. Magnesium oxide is similar in structure to sodium chloride. The crystalline aluminium oxide is known as corundum, in which oxygen ions form nearly hexagonal close-packed structure with the aluminium ions.

Tidbit

Corundum, naturally occurring aluminum oxide mineral (Al₂O₃) that is, after diamond, the hardest known natural substance.

Silicon dioxide is covalent oxide having giant structure. There are three different crystal forms of silicon dioxide; the most suitable structure is similar to that of diamond.

Phosphorus, sulphur and chlorine form molecular oxides. Some of these molecules are simple, while others are polymeric. Thus, the trend in structure in period is

Giant metallic ionic oxides → giant covalent oxide → molecular oxide.

13.1.3.2 Melting and Boiling Points

The giant structures (the metal oxides and silicon dioxide) have high melting points and boiling points because a lot of energy is needed to break the strong bonds (ionic or covalent) operating in their lattices. The oxides of phosphorus, sulphur and chlorine consist of individual molecules, some small and simple, others polymeric.

The attractive forces between these molecules will be dispersion forces and dipole-dipole interactions. The strength of the attractive forces depend on the size, shape and polarity of various molecules but are always much weaker than the ionic or covalent bonds present in a giant structure. These oxides are gases, liquids or low – melting solids.

Table 13.8 Melting and Boiling Points of Period 3ʳᵈ Oxides

13.1.3.3 Electrical Conductivity

None of the period 3ʳᵈ oxides have any free or mobile electrons. It means that none of them will conduct electricity when they are in solid state. The ionic oxides can, however, conduct electricity in molten state because of the movement of ions towards the opposite electrodes.

13.1.4 Acid-Base Behaviour of the Oxides

Going across period 3, from left to right the nature of the oxides changes from basic (Na₂O,MgO) to amphoteric (Al₂O₃) and then to acidic (SiO₂,P₄O₆/P₄O₁₀,SO₂/SO₃). The acidity of the oxides increases across the period.

13.1.3 آکسائیڈز کی طبعی خصوصیات

تیسرے دور کے عناصر کے آکسائیڈز درج ذیل ہیں۔

اوپر کی قطار کے آکسائیڈز میں تیسرے دور کے عناصر اپنی سب سے بلند تکسیدی حالت میں ہیں۔ ان میں عناصر کے تمام بیرونی الیکٹران بند بنانے میں شامل ہیں: سوڈیم کے صرف ایک الیکٹران سے لے کر Cl₂O₇ میں کلورین کے ساتوں بیرونی الیکٹرانوں تک۔

سوڈیم، میگنیشیم، ایلومینیم، سلیکان اور فاسفورس کے بلند تکسیدی حالت والے آکسائیڈز ٹھوس ہیں، جبکہ سلفر اور کلورین کے آکسائیڈز مائع ہیں۔ سلفر اور کلورین کے کم تکسیدی حالت والے آکسائیڈز گیس حالت میں ہیں۔

13.1.3.1 ساخت

سوڈیم، میگنیشیم اور ایلومینیم کے آکسائیڈز بڑی ساختوں پر مشتمل ہیں، جن میں دھاتی اور آکسائیڈ آئن ہوتے ہیں۔ میگنیشیم آکسائیڈ کی ساخت سوڈیم کلورائیڈ جیسی ہے۔ قلمی ایلومینیم آکسائیڈ کورنڈم کہلاتی ہے، جس میں آکسیجن کے آئن ایلومینیم آئنوں کے ساتھ تقریباً مسدسی قریب قریب بھری ہوئی ساخت بناتے ہیں۔

13.1.3.2 پگھلنے اور ابلنے کے درجے

بڑی ساختوں (دھاتی آکسائیڈز اور سلیکان ڈائی آکسائیڈ) کے پگھلنے اور ابلنے کے درجے زیادہ ہیں، کیونکہ ان کی جالیوں کے مضبوط آئنک یا اشتراکی بند توڑنے کے لیے بہت توانائی درکار ہوتی ہے۔ فاسفورس، سلفر اور کلورین کے آکسائیڈز الگ الگ سالموں پر مشتمل ہیں؛ کچھ چھوٹے اور سادہ، دوسرے کثیر سالماتی ہیں۔

ان سالموں کے درمیان کششی قوتیں انتشار کی قوتیں اور دو قطبی تعاملات ہوتی ہیں۔ ان کی طاقت مختلف سالموں کی جسامت، شکل اور قطبیت پر منحصر ہے، مگر بڑی ساخت کے آئنک یا اشتراکی بندوں سے ہمیشہ بہت کمزور ہوتی ہے۔ یہ آکسائیڈز گیسیں، مائعات یا کم نقطۂ پگھلاؤ والے ٹھوس مادے ہیں۔

Society, Technology And Science

Body need a certain amount of iodine in order to make a chemical known as thyroid hormone. Thyroid hormone controls body metabolism and other important functions in the body.

Iodine is found primarily in seawater and in the soil especially in coastal areas. At high elevations, iodine is often deficient in the water and soil. Lack of iodine can cause an abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as a goitre.

A goitre is an abnormal enlargement of thyroid gland. Thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland located at the base of neck. The most common cause of goitres worldwide is a lack of iodine in the diet. Iodine deficiency may be made worse by a diet high in hormone-inhibiting foods, such as cabbage, broccoli and cauliflower.

Our body does not naturally make iodine, so the only way to get this nutrient is through diet. Adults typically require 150μg per day. Pregnant and breastfeeding women need 200μg per day.

13.1.3 Physical Properties of the Oxides

The oxides of period 3ʳᵈ elements are following.

The oxides in the top row are the oxides where period 3 elements are in their highest oxidation state. In these oxides, all the outer electrons in period 3 elements are being involved in bonding from just one in sodium to all seven outer electrons of chlorine in Cl₂O₇.

The oxides (high oxidation state) of sodium, magnesium, aluminium, silicon, phosphorous are in solid state and those of sulphur and chlorine are in liquid state. The oxides having low oxidation state of sulphur and chlorine are in gaseous state.

13.1.3.1 Structure

Sodium, magnesium and aluminium oxides consist of giant structures containing metal ions and oxide ions. Magnesium oxide is similar in structure to sodium chloride. The crystalline aluminium oxide is known as corundum, in which oxygen ions form nearly hexagonal close-packed structure with the aluminium ions.

Tidbit

Corundum, naturally occurring aluminum oxide mineral (Al₂O₃) that is, after diamond, the hardest known natural substance.

Silicon dioxide is covalent oxide having giant structure. There are three different crystal forms of silicon dioxide; the most suitable structure is similar to that of diamond.

Phosphorus, sulphur and chlorine form molecular oxides. Some of these molecules are simple, while others are polymeric. Thus, the trend in structure in period is

Giant metallic ionic oxides → giant covalent oxide → molecular oxide.

13.1.3.2 Melting and Boiling Points

The giant structures (the metal oxides and silicon dioxide) have high melting points and boiling points because a lot of energy is needed to break the strong bonds (ionic or covalent) operating in their lattices. The oxides of phosphorus, sulphur and chlorine consist of individual molecules, some small and simple, others polymeric.

The attractive forces between these molecules will be dispersion forces and dipole-dipole interactions. The strength of the attractive forces depend on the size, shape and polarity of various molecules but are always much weaker than the ionic or covalent bonds present in a giant structure. These oxides are gases, liquids or low – melting solids.

Table 13.8 Melting and Boiling Points of Period 3ʳᵈ Oxides

13.1.3.3 Electrical Conductivity

None of the period 3ʳᵈ oxides have any free or mobile electrons. It means that none of them will conduct electricity when they are in solid state. The ionic oxides can, however, conduct electricity in molten state because of the movement of ions towards the opposite electrodes.

13.1.4 Acid-Base Behaviour of the Oxides

Going across period 3, from left to right the nature of the oxides changes from basic (Na₂O,MgO) to amphoteric (Al₂O₃) and then to acidic (SiO₂,P₄O₆/P₄O₁₀,SO₂/SO₃). The acidity of the oxides increases across the period.
